title: Treaty of Shimoda
summary: The English Wikipedia article "Treaty of Shimoda", at revision 1380617744, opens: "The Treaty of Shimoda , formally the Treaty of Commerce and Navigation between Japan and Russia , was the first treaty between the Russian Empire and the Empire of Japan, signed on February 7, 1855. Signed shortly after the Convention of Kanagawa between Japan and the United States, it effectively meant the end of Japan's 220-year-old policy of national seclusion (sakoku) by opening the ports of Nagasaki, Shimoda and Hakodate to Russian vessels. The treaty also established the position of Russian consuls in Japan and defined the borders between Japan and Russia." That is the article's account and not yet this atlas's; nobody has read this record, and review.html is where somebody does. Wikidata item Q497189, imported by tools/import/wikidata.mjs. The item's own description reads "treaty between the Russian Empire, and the Empire of Japan (Tokugawa shogunate)". Everything here is copied from the item's own fields and nothing in it is this atlas's account of the thing: that is still to be written, and review.html is where somebody writes it.
